# AltBins.pro

> Free, open-source (MIT) desktop utilities for Windows, macOS and Linux by Ivan Poluianov. On Windows and Linux each utility is a single portable executable with no installer and no dependencies; on macOS it is a signed and notarized .dmg for Apple Silicon. Linux builds are x64 and arm64, also as .deb and .rpm packages and a one-line install script.

Downloads come from the GitHub releases of each project. Every app has a light and a dark theme; AltPing and AltHex speak 12 languages, AltSysInfo 31, AltSerialPort English and Russian.

The idea is software that is easy to install: download one file, run it, and it works. The apps are written in Go and compiled to native code: no Electron, no .NET or Java runtime, no background services.

- Install is optional on Windows and Linux. On Windows the Install link in the status bar copies the .exe into `%USERPROFILE%\.altbins` and adds it to the Start menu, the desktop and "Installed apps"; remove it there or with the Uninstall link. On Linux the one-line install puts the binary into `~/.altbins` for the current user without root and adds a menu entry; remove it with Uninstall in the menu entry or `~/.altbins/.<app>-uninstall.sh`. The .deb and .rpm packages are removed with the package manager. On macOS drag the app to Applications, and to the Trash to remove it.
- Settings, lists and history live in `~/.altbins/.<app>` in the home folder (`%USERPROFILE%\.altbins\.<app>` on Windows). Uninstalling leaves them; delete the folder to reset the app or clean up.
- The apps collect no statistics and send nothing anywhere unless the user asks. AltPing contacts only the hosts the user adds and publishes a host's ping time to u00.io only when that is turned on. The AltHex API and MCP server are off until switched on and listen only on the local machine. AltSysInfo only reads information about the computer and sends it nowhere.
- Building needs only the Go compiler, no cgo: `git clone https://github.com/ipoluianov/<app> && cd <app> && go build .` Without cgo, every platform builds from any other (`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -ldflags=-H=windowsgui .`). `build/all.sh` in each repository builds all release files.

Full text of all docs in one file: [llms-full.txt](https://altbins.pro/llms-full.txt). Each docs page also has a Markdown copy at `index.md` next to it.

## AltPing

Network ping utility with a GUI. It pings a list of hosts every second and shows the ping time, plus loss, average and maximum over the last 5 minutes, with a 24-hour history chart. It can check a TCP port instead of ping, logs downtime, beeps or shows a desktop notification when a host goes down, keeps running in the tray, exports history to CSV and can publish a host's live ping to a public page on u00.io. Works without root on Linux and macOS (unprivileged ICMP / UDP mode).

- [AltPing](https://altbins.pro/altping/): overview, features and screenshot
- [AltPing docs](https://altbins.pro/altping/docs/index.md): table columns, colors, history chart, host lists, settings, keyboard shortcuts (Markdown)
- [AltPing for Windows](https://altbins.pro/altping/windows/): portable .exe (x64)
- [AltPing for macOS](https://altbins.pro/altping/macos/): signed .dmg (Apple Silicon)
- [AltPing for Linux](https://altbins.pro/altping/linux/): portable binary, .deb, .rpm, one-line install, notes on ping without root
- [Source code](https://github.com/ipoluianov/altping): GitHub, MIT license

## AltHex

Hex editor for files of any size, disks, disk images and firmware. A 50 GB file opens at once because only the visible parts are read; edits are written on save, with unlimited undo. It recognizes PNG, ELF, PE, ZIP, PDF, MBR, GPT, FAT, NTFS, ext4 and more and shows their fields as an editable tree; custom formats are described in a C-like template language close to 010 Editor Binary Templates. It compares files (even with shifts) and makes or applies IPS, BPS and text patches; computes CRC-8 to CRC-64, Adler-32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, BLAKE3, entropy and byte histograms; opens disks read-only; and disassembles firmware (Intel HEX, S-record, UF2, DfuSe, ESP images; ARM, AVR, RISC-V, Xtensa, x86). AI agents and programs can use it over MCP and a local JSON-RPC 2.0 API; there is also a command line for batch jobs.

- [AltHex](https://altbins.pro/althex/): overview, features and screenshots
- [AltHex user guide](https://altbins.pro/althex/docs/index.md): common tasks, editing, navigation, import and export, recovery, boot images, settings, keys (Markdown)
- [AltHex template language](https://altbins.pro/althex/docs/templates/index.md): types, byte order, arrays, structs, enums, bit fields, attributes, built-in functions (Markdown)
- [AltHex MCP and local API](https://altbins.pro/althex/docs/api/index.md): connecting an AI agent (`claude mcp add althex -- althex mcp`), JSON-RPC methods, the list of tools and their arguments (Markdown)
- [AltHex for Windows](https://altbins.pro/althex/windows/): portable .exe (x64)
- [AltHex for macOS](https://altbins.pro/althex/macos/): signed .dmg (Apple Silicon)
- [AltHex for Linux](https://altbins.pro/althex/linux/): portable binary, .deb, .rpm, one-line install
- [Source code](https://github.com/ipoluianov/althex): GitHub, MIT license

## AltSysInfo

Hardware and system information viewer with a GUI. It shows the CPU, memory modules, drives and volumes, graphics adapters and displays, network adapters, PCI and USB devices, audio, sensors and battery, sorted into 12 categories. Any value is copied with one click; the CPU, memory, drives and graphics are saved as a PDF report. A built-in PCI ID database finds a vendor or device by ID or name without the internet. Works without root on Linux (reads /proc, /sys and udev; memory modules may need root when udev has no data). 31 languages.

- [AltSysInfo](https://altbins.pro/altsysinfo/): overview, features and screenshot
- [AltSysInfo docs](https://altbins.pro/altsysinfo/docs/index.md): categories, copying values, PDF report, PCI ID lookup, tray, settings, keyboard shortcuts (Markdown)
- [AltSysInfo for Windows](https://altbins.pro/altsysinfo/windows/): portable .exe (x64)
- [AltSysInfo for macOS](https://altbins.pro/altsysinfo/macos/): signed .dmg (Apple Silicon)
- [AltSysInfo for Linux](https://altbins.pro/altsysinfo/linux/): portable binary, .deb, .rpm, one-line install
- [Source code](https://github.com/ipoluianov/altsysinfo): GitHub, MIT license

## AltSerialPort

Serial port terminal for low-level debugging of hardware: microcontroller boards, USB-UART adapters, modems, GPS and industrial devices. Lists ports with their chips (CH340, CP2102…), reopens the port after a board reset, re-flash or pulled cable, any baud rate and frame, changed on the open port. Text (ANSI colors), Hex and Mixed views with timestamps down to microseconds; keys sent as in a console, commands with history, escapes, hex bytes and checksums (CRC-16 Modbus, CCITT, XMODEM, CRC-8, CRC-32, XOR, Sum, LRC); DTR/RTS switching, BREAK, Arduino/ESP32 reset. Logging, live plots of numbers in the data, macros, highlight rules and triggers, a second port and a bridge (also to TCP), statistics, baud rate detection, XMODEM/YMODEM file transfer, profiles. Network ports tcp://, tcp-listen://, rfc2217://; RS-485 mode on Linux. Command line (`altserialport list`, a console terminal, `altserialport send … --expect OK`) and an MCP server (`claude mcp add altserialport -- altserialport mcp`) for AI agents to work with a real board. On Linux the user must be in the dialout group.

- [AltSerialPort](https://altbins.pro/altserialport/): overview and features
- [AltSerialPort docs](https://altbins.pro/altserialport/docs/index.md): ports, views, sending, lines, logs, tools, keyboard shortcuts, command line, MCP (Markdown)
- [AltSerialPort for Windows](https://altbins.pro/altserialport/windows/): portable .exe (x64)
- [AltSerialPort for macOS](https://altbins.pro/altserialport/macos/): signed .dmg (Apple Silicon)
- [AltSerialPort for Linux](https://altbins.pro/altserialport/linux/): portable binary, .deb, .rpm, one-line install, dialout group
- [Source code](https://github.com/ipoluianov/altserialport): GitHub, MIT license

## Author

Ivan Poluianov, a software engineer with more than 20 years of experience in commercial software: industrial SCADA systems, and software and firmware for laboratory analytical instruments such as mass spectrometers and gas chromatographs. Skills: Go, C/C++, C# / .NET, Assembler, STM32, databases.

- [Author on GitHub](https://github.com/ipoluianov)
